hyps.why: Edge 4 is fed by edge 0, so when edge 0 is none the 0->1->3 path is dead and a conv on edge 4 adds little.
Edge 5 is fed by edge 1, so when edge 1 is none that path through node 2 is weakened and the conv helps less.
Edge 2 only carries signal if edge 0 is active, so a conv on it has no effect when edge 0 is none.
Replacing a conv on the direct edge with skip loses capacity, while replacing none with skip gains a lot.
Removing a conv edge hurts much more than removing an already weak op.
Replacing none with a conv gives a large gain, but replacing a stronger op gives a smaller gain or a loss.
Cutting a conv on the first edge, which feeds two paths, costs far more than cutting a pool or skip edge.
Turning a dead edge into a conv adds a new learnable path, a bigger gain than upgrading an existing op.
Swapping a conv for a pool is a downgrade, whereas replacing none with a pool is roughly neutral or positive.
Adding a conv to a removed direct edge gives more gain than replacing skip or pool, which already help trainability.
